title: Introduce the world (0-12 minutes):
use_cases: Use when drafting the opening 0-12 minutes of a horror screenplay
Implement when establishing the protagonist's normal world and internal weaknesses
Configure when deciding whether to include an upfront teaser to pique audience interest
Use when building early tension through environmental clues and foreshadowing
Implement when integrating backstory elements without utilizing late-stage exposition
content:
OPTIONAL Horror teaser or introduction — some horror films start with a short, sharp shock such as a murder or another violent incident, which will remain unexplained until later on. Others with a brief introduction or fragment of backstory. Such opening scenes can add a bit of up-front bite, or pique audience interest, provided they don’t give away too much.

Show the world of your story as it normally is — introduce the protagonist, key characters and the setting. Signal any emotional vulnerability or psychological flaw in the main character so that it can be used against them later by your film’s horror elements.

Foreshadow the horror — small hints or clues that suggest all is not well, e.g., weird sounds, disquieting imagery.

Example: In “Haunt” (2013), there is a brief horror teaser and an introduction: Franklin Morello tries to communicate with his dead children in the afterlife using a spirit box and is attacked, possessed, and killed by an as-yet unexplained malevolent supernatural entity. Franklin’s widow then informs the audience in voiceover that her entire family died in mysterious circumstances and there is a curse on her house. These two elements could have been woven into later parts of the film in the form of flashbacks or expository dialogue, but they work well at the beginning, providing clarity without giving away too much.

Then the film ‘really’ starts: we are introduced to the protagonist, Evan, and meet his family as they move into the so-called Morello house.

A flickering lightbulb, a loose floorboard, and the creepy portrait of a dead boy soon confirm that not all is well in Evan’s new home, foreshadowing the horror to come.
